QuantumBridge — Live Circuit Reliability Predictor

Pick a real IBM chip layout and any two qubits, and get a Bell-pair circuit's predicted execution success from two models: v4.1, a hand-derived closed-form physics model, and GNN, a graph neural network. All three chips' predictions now come from one unified model trained on Kyiv, Sherbrooke, and Brisbane data pooled together, with a calibrated MC-Dropout uncertainty band (shown as ±) validated on a held-out split before deployment (Entry 071). Where available, the actual simulated hardware result is shown alongside for comparison.
40,005 qubit pairs covered (5 chips) 6,398 circuits in combined training data 127 qubits per chip (Kyiv, Sherbrooke, Brisbane, Osaka & Quebec) 2,737 GNN parameters Quebec is a true zero-shot holdout, never trained on

What this is, honestly: every prediction shown is a real output from the actual trained model and the actual closed-form formula — nothing here is faked or approximated for the demo. But the underlying noise data comes from Qiskit's "fake backend" snapshots of real IBM device calibration, run through Aer's noise simulator — not live queued jobs on physical hardware. Ground truth is only available for the subset of pairs that were actually simulated (about 5,250 of the 40,005 shown here across all five chips); the rest show model predictions only, clearly marked. The ± range next to the GNN prediction is a genuine uncertainty estimate (MC-Dropout, 20 stochastic forward passes per pair) from one unified model trained across four chips -- it widens on circuit types and chip regions the model is less confident about, not a cosmetic error bar, and calibration was checked on a genuine held-out split before deployment. This is an early-stage academic project (undergraduate research), not a production tool. Built with Qiskit, JAX/Optax, and a from-scratch graph neural network. Each prediction is marked live (computed fresh by a real backend, Entry 074) or cached (served from the precomputed table), except Quebec, which always shows zero-shot / never trained since it is deliberately excluded from training -- the demo automatically uses the live backend when one is configured and reachable, and falls back to the precomputed table otherwise, so it always works either way.
